card.decision: Should punctuation count toward a word's length, so that 'done.' has length 5 and beats 'hello' only when it is longer?

experts.why: Keeps one definition of 'word' shared with word_count; a test pins the behaviour.
Matches the existing word definition in the library; a better definition can be a separate ticket.
Not a contract conflict if documented; the docstring should state that punctuation stays attached.

options.consequence: Reuses words() as is, consistent with word_count. 'hello,' can beat 'hello'; the docstring must say so and a test pins it. Can be changed later with a new helper.

ticket.purpose: Add a new module `src/longest.py` with `longest_word(text)` returning the longest word in `text`. Reuse the existing `words` helper from `src/textstats.py`.
ticket.title: Add longest_word

card.while_waiting: This ticket is parked at plan; other tickets continue.
card.why: words() splits on whitespace only, so 'hello,' is 6 characters and 'a-b' is one word. Punctuation changes which word wins the length comparison and what longest_word returns (for example 'world,' rather than 'world').
